draft_selected.headline: Astra edits model weights without retraining
draft_selected.summary: MIT CSAIL researchers report that GPT-6 Astra can inspect, write and repair neural-network weights directly. In one experiment, it changed 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B’s weights, reducing reasoning loops and raising reported MATH-500 accuracy from 7.9% to 48.1% without gradient descent, while the authors stress the work remains early and inefficient.
draft_selected.why_it_matters: Direct weight editing could become a targeted repair tool, but the evidence is still a controlled research result. Teams should reproduce the claimed gains, inspect regressions and compare compute costs before treating it as an alternative to training.
draft_selected.read_scope: Full original project post, experiment setup, reported benchmark table, controls, limitations and future-work section.

draft_selected.headline: StateBench exposes long-horizon tracking failures
draft_selected.summary: Ai2’s StateBench tests whether language models can track evolving states across long sequences in six finite-system tasks. The authors report that frontier models fall to 13% accuracy or less on the longest general cases, while directly trained recurrent and hybrid models generalize farther under the benchmark’s fixed-variable conditions.
draft_selected.why_it_matters: Long tool chains and agent workflows depend on remembering what changed, not merely generating plausible next steps. Use this benchmark pattern to stress-test state transitions, while noting that fixed variable counts and numerical precision leave important deployment conditions untested.
draft_selected.read_scope: Full original article covering six tasks, long-horizon results, recurrent/hybrid comparison and stated benchmark constraints.

draft_selected.headline: OpenAI’s hardware agent designs a device in weeks
draft_selected.summary: OpenAI says its Astra engineering agent produced an enclosure, circuit board, interface and firmware for a portable device without direct human edits. A prototype arrived in under a week and a small batch within a month, but manufacturer review still found tolerance, assembly and verification gaps that required expert judgment.
draft_selected.why_it_matters: The case shows where autonomous engineering may compress iteration and where it still needs manufacturing review. Hardware teams can separate agent-generated artifacts from approval checkpoints, then measure rework, safety findings and prototype lead time against a conventional process.
draft_selected.read_scope: Full original case study including artifacts, timing, manufacturer review, BenchCAD results and human-review limits.

draft_selected.headline: Palette trains a small model to build branded decks
draft_selected.summary: IBM Research describes Palette, a 20-billion-parameter open model trained on about 1,000 presentations and 10,000 slides. A designer component emits structured plans, a coder writes PptxGenJS, and automated overlap and overflow checks trigger repairs. On PresentBench, IBM reports the checking harness improved results by 3.5 points.
draft_selected.why_it_matters: Presentation automation becomes more useful when layout errors are treated as test failures instead of cosmetic surprises. Teams can borrow the planner–coder–checker pattern, but should evaluate brand fidelity, accessibility and complex-chart handling on their own deck library.
draft_selected.read_scope: Full original article covering training set, designer/coder architecture, PptxGenJS checks, PresentBench and limitations.

draft_selected.headline: Meet can show policy notices before Gemini notes
draft_selected.summary: Google Workspace now lets administrators show custom policy text before users join Google Meet calls, either always or only when recording, transcription or Gemini note-taking is active. The setting is off by default, can include a policy link and can be applied by organizational unit during the extended rollout.
draft_selected.why_it_matters: A visible pre-join notice puts governance at the moment an AI meeting feature is used. Administrators can pair the message with a durable policy page, choose the right organizational scope and confirm that guests see the host’s notice.
draft_selected.read_scope: Complete original update plus administrator help steps, rollout, scope, defaults and guest-notice behavior.
draft_selected.audience_fit: A noncoding administrator can govern recording, transcription and AI notes at the moment employees and guests join a meeting.

draft_selected.headline: Use a three-check brief before delegating to an agent
draft_selected.summary: Every’s November 1 roundup turns a week of agent experiments into practical delegation habits: ask what useful work the agent can do that you have not tried, require the source and last-updated date for its answer, and choose the final format before drafting. The sequence creates a reusable agent briefing skill.
draft_selected.why_it_matters: This skill helps uncover overlooked delegation opportunities without accepting unsupported output. Run the three checks on one bounded task, record the evidence and requested format, then compare whether the result reduced rework or surfaced a genuinely useful workflow.
draft_selected.read_scope: Complete original weekly roundup, linked practice descriptions, source-check prompts, delegation examples and limitations.
draft_selected.audience_fit: A nontechnical knowledge worker can run the three checks on a bounded task using ordinary chat and existing work documents.

agent_skill.name: Three-check agent brief
agent_skill.distinct_action: Ask for an untried useful task, require its source and last-updated date, then specify the delivery format before drafting.
agent_skill.reader_outcome: A bounded, evidence-aware delegation brief whose usefulness and rework can be compared with the prior workflow.
